content.text:
I have what I need. The analysis:

- **§14 (p0079)**: Client has an unconditional right to terminate on written notice, with services continuing only until the last day of the month following the notice month (~30–60 days' effective notice). No early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in the document.
- **§13 (p0078)**: Initial term is 1 year, auto-renewing in 1-year increments; TrueLink has **no** mid-term convenience exit — only a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice at the end of each annual term.
- **§5 (p0045)**: Fees are invoiced monthly and paid within 15 days of receipt (arrears), so there are no prepaid fees requiring a pro-rata refund.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position on both material terms. (1) Customer convenience right: Section 14 (p0079) lets Client terminate at will on written notice, with services simply running to the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective 30–60 days' notice, well inside the preferred 30-day / fallback 60–90 day window. No early-termination fee, penalty or liquidated damages appears anywhere in the document. (2) No Vendor convenience exit: Section 13 (p0078) sets a one-year term with automatic one-year renewals; TrueLink has no right to walk mid-term for convenience (its only unilateral cut-off is the automatic termination of Sections 2 and 3 on a Client breach or a breach of Sections 8a–8c, which is cause-based, not convenience). The term is 12 months, so the "no convenience right in a multi-year term" walk-away does not arise, and Client in any event has one. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the model language and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is largely moot because Section 5a (p0045) bills Hosting and Support Services monthly with invoices paid 15 days after receipt (i.e., in arrears, so little or nothing is prepaid); and the end-of-term non-renewal notice in Section 13 is 30 days rather than the 90 days contemplated for a Vendor end-of-term exit. That non-renewal right is mutual and operates only at natural expiry of a one-year term, not as a mid-term convenience termination, and shortening it would equally cut back our own flexibility — so we do not redline it. Section 14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 4 is not included in the reviewed text, but the cross-references in Section 5/6 (p0047) indicate Section 4 concerns minimum monthly fees rather than any limit on the termination right; worth confirming on receipt of the full Section 4.
